# Video Capture Manual

How footage for the intro video is actually made on this machine. Written so a cold session
— or a future you — can reshoot any shot without rediscovering anything.

**The premise:** the video is built like code. Every shot is generated by a script, so fixing
a bubble, changing a word, or reshooting one beat is an edit and a re-run, not an afternoon.
That only holds if the *how* is written down. This is the how.

Companions: [production_plan.md](production_plan.md) (what we're
shooting and why), [language.md](language.md) (copy),
[../tools/intro_video/README.md](../../tools/intro_video/README.md) (the web-capture tool).

---

## 0. Naming discipline

Two unrelated things are both called "the emulator". Confusing them wastes real time.

| Term used here | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **Android emulator** / **AVD** | The virtual phone. `emulator-5554`, driven by `adb`. |
| **Firebase emulators** | Local firestore/functions on ports 8080–8083 / 5001–5004. |

Always say which. When a doc or a commit message says just "emulator", assume it's wrong.

---

## 1. The rigs

> **2026-08-28: the sign-in sequence moved entirely inside the Android emulator.**
> Chrome and the identity app on one device, shot as a single continuous take
> against **production**. That removed every fiction at once — the drawn browser
> bar, the substituted `keymeid` transport, the localhost-vs-nerdster.org gap, and
> the two-rigs-cut-together seam. See §9.
>
> Rig A is still right for shots that are *only* a web app (feed browsing, PoV
> switching, trust modes) — it's faster, scriptable, and has the styled finger
> overlay. Use the AVD when the browser itself is part of the story.

| Rig | Used for | Capture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A. Web app** | Nerdster, HabloTengo — page-only shots | Playwright headless Chromium, phone-sized viewport |
| **B. Phone app** | ONE-OF-US.NET identity app | Android emulator + `adb screenrecord` |
| **C. In-device** | Anything involving the browser as a *thing*: sign-in handoff, tabs, copy/paste, URL entry | Chrome **inside** the AVD, one continuous `adb screenrecord` |

## 2. Rig A — web apps (Nerdster, HabloTengo)

The tool: [../tools/intro_video/](../../tools/intro_video/). Read its README too; this section
is the part that isn't obvious from the code.

```bash
cd ~/src/github/oneofus/tools/intro_video
npm install && npx playwright install chromium ffmpeg   # first time only
node record_nerdster.js --scene identity-bar --pov milhouse   # not committed
./build.sh milhouse_identity-bar captions/milhouse_identity_bar.ass
```

### Phone size at full resolution

432×768 CSS viewport gives the app its **phone layout**; the browser is launched with
`--force-device-scale-factor=2.5`, so output pixels are **1080×1920**.

> **Force DPI at the browser, never the context.** Playwright's context-level
> `deviceScaleFactor` is silently dropped partway through a recording when Flutter re-creates
> its canvas: the video continues at 1×, with the app in the top-left quarter of the frame
> and grey everywhere else. Cost a whole take before it was spotted.

### Driving it

- **Real touch, not mouse.** Gestures go through CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`, so Flutter
  applies its own fling physics — the scroll accelerates and settles like a phone. A mouse
  wheel scrolls at constant velocity and reads wrong on screen.
- `mouse.wheel` does nothing unless the pointer is first parked over the scrollable area
  (it defaults to 0,0, which is the toolbar). Silent no-op.
- The Identity-bar submenu **does not open on mouse click** — only on hover. It *does* open
  on tap, exactly as on a real phone. Another reason to drive with touch.
- Coordinates are hardcoded CSS pixels for the 432×768 viewport. If the viewport or the
  toolbar layout changes, re-probe with a screenshot. **A wrong tap fails silently and looks
  like a hang.**

### Point of view without signing in

```
https://nerdster.org/app?pov=<url-encoded public key JSON>
```

The same mechanism as nerdster.org's own "Milhouse's view" button (`web/home.js` in the
nerdster repo). Public key, public data, no private key anywhere in the tooling. Add
`&fire=emulator` to read the Firebase emulators instead of production.

### Serving a local build

| Script | What it does | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nerdster/bin/serve_web.sh` | release `flutter build web`, restructures, serves **:8765** | final takes |
| `nerdster/bin/run_dev.sh` | `flutter run -d chrome --web-port=8765`, hot reload | iterating |

`run_dev.sh` is much lighter and Playwright can still load `localhost:8765`, but it's a debug
build and renders more jankily — fine for finding coordinates, not for footage.

> **CWD trap.** The shell resets to the primary working directory between commands. Running
> `./bin/serve_web.sh` without `cd`-ing first started *hablotengo's* server and served the
> wrong app on the wrong port, and two tests were run against it before anyone noticed.
> Always `cd` explicitly, and check which app answered.

### Marks and trimming

`record_nerdster.js` writes `out/<name>.marks.json` with a timestamp per beat. `build.sh`
trims on those marks rather than hand-timed offsets, so the trim follows the take.

> Rig A's files (`record_nerdster.js`, `build.sh`, `bubbles.js`, `captions/`, the VO
> scripts) are kept on disk but **not committed** — only the sign-in pipeline is. They work,
> but they haven't been through the cleanup the sign-in rig has.

## 3. Rig B — the ONE-OF-US.NET app (Android emulator)

### Starting the AVD

```bash
flutter emulators --launch Pixel_3a_API_35
```

Screen is **1080×2220**. For a 1080×1920 timeline: `crop=1080:1920:0:150` (drops the status
bar and the gesture bar, keeps scale identical to the web footage so both halves look like
the same phone).

> **If capture returns wallpaper, restart the AVD.** One instance had dead display readback:
> `adb screencap`, `adb screenrecord` and `scrcpy` all returned stale wallpaper frames while
> `dumpsys` said the app was foreground and `logcat` showed it rendering at a steady 60fps.
> Nothing was wrong with the app or the tooling. Relaunching the AVD fixed it completely.
> Recognise it by: three different capture tools agreeing, and logcat showing
> `EGL_emulation: app_time_stats: avg=16.6ms` — i.e. it *is* drawing.

### Capturing

```bash
adb exec-out screencap -p > shot.png                                   # still
adb shell screenrecord --time-limit 60 --bit-rate 8000000 /sdcard/x.mp4
adb pull /sdcard/x.mp4
```

`screenrecord` caps at 180s. Visible taps come from Android itself:

```bash
adb shell settings put system show_touches 1
```

That's a plain dot — not the styled blob the web overlay draws (that's DOM injection, so
web-only). Matching the two is an open problem.

> **scrcpy is a snap and cannot write outside `$HOME`.** It prints "Recording started" and
> produces a **0-byte file** with no error. Record to `~/Videos/…`, never `/tmp`.

### Building and installing the app

```bash
cd ~/src/github/oneofus
flutter build apk --debug
adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk
```

> **Version downgrade.** A debug build is versionCode 1. If a Play-store build is installed
> (e.g. 49), `install -r` fails with `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE` and you must
> `adb uninstall` first — **which destroys the identity on that device.** `install -r`
> between two debug builds preserves data.

> **Which backend the app writes to is hardcoded** in `lib/core/config.dart`:
> `static final FireChoice _fireChoice = FireChoice.prod;`
> There is no dart-define. For filming, flip it to `FireChoice.emulator`, build, install,
> then **revert the source immediately** so the change can't ship. The installed APK keeps
> the filming setting; the tree stays clean. A red dot in the app's top bar indicates
> non-prod.

### AVD disk

6 GB `/data`, and it runs near full. Symptom: `INSTALL_FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE`
(a debug APK is ~100 MB and installation needs roughly double).

```bash
adb shell pm trim-caches 999G     # this is usually enough
```

> **Editing `disk.dataPartition.size` in `~/.android/avd/<name>.avd/config.ini` does NOT
> grow an existing AVD.** Tried it — 6 GB → 12 GB, cold boot, still 5.8 GB. Growing a live
> userdata image needs a wipe (destroys the identity) or an image-level resize. Unsolved.

## 4. Rig C — the cross-app sign-in, entirely in the emulator

**AVD Chrome is fast enough.** Measured 2026-08-28 on `Pixel_3a_API_35`, no memory
bump needed: the Nerdster (Flutter/canvaskit) loads fully in ~10s and scrolls at
**28.7 unique fps** (342 unique of 479 captured frames over 11.9s). Earlier
assumption that this would be prohibitive was wrong, and it cost a day of building
a drawn browser bar that has since been deleted.

### Why this rig wins

Chrome and the identity app on one device means the *real* things happen: real URL
bar that updates on navigation, real universal link opening the app, real tabs,
real copy/paste, one continuous recording with no seam. And shooting against
production means real data and real signatures.

### Setup

```bash
# the app is debug-signed, so app-link verification fails (pm get-app-links
# shows state 1024). Approve it by hand — a rig setting, not a code change:
adb shell pm set-app-links-user-selection --user 0 \
  --package net.oneofus.app true one-of-us.net
```

Build the app for **production** (the default `fireChoice`) with filming tools:

```bash
flutter build apk --debug --dart-define=filmTools=true
adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk
```

### Running it

```bash
cd tools/intro_video
adb -s emulator-5554 forward tcp:9222 localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote
node reset_browser.js
node shoot_signin.js
node overlay_taps.js out/signin_<stamp>.mp4
```

About nine seconds of finished video, `out/signin_<stamp>_taps.mp4`.

### It can see the screen

Flutter draws to a canvas, so nothing is queryable: taps become hardcoded pixels,
waits become tuned sleeps, and a take that hits the wrong dialog still records a
perfectly valid file of the wrong thing. All three happened, repeatedly.

Flutter also keeps an accessibility tree. `lib/semantics.js` turns it on and uses
it, so the script taps *"https://one-of-us.net/…"* rather than a coordinate, waits
until a dialog exists, and asserts the expected screen before continuing. A bad
take now stops with a message naming what was actually on screen.

Chrome inside the AVD is reached over `adb forward tcp:9222
localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote`, so the same helpers drive it.

> **Enable it with a real touch at the placeholder's CENTRE.** A synthetic
> `.click()` works in desktop Chromium and does nothing in Chrome on Android, and
> the placeholder reports a viewport-sized box but only responds near its middle —
> a corner tap silently yields zero nodes.

> **Re-inject after navigation.** The probe lives in the document; navigating from
> the home page to `/app` wipes it, and the CDP session must be re-acquired
> against the new target or its input events go nowhere.

### The reset — three places, not two

A take needs *vouched, no delegate*, or the app offers to rotate an existing
delegate instead of creating one:

| # | State | Where | Reset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | delegate **statement** | published, one-of-us.net | `node truncate_statements.js --token <t> --project oneofus --prod --keep <first>` with `I_MEAN_IT=yes` |
| 2 | delegate **key** | identity app secure storage | `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "keymeid://deletekey?domain=nerdster.org"` |
| 3 | **identity + delegate in the browser** | page storage, "Store keys" is ticked | `node reset_browser.js` |

**#3 silently ruins takes** — the app never prompts because the browser is already
signed in.

> Resetting #3 through the UI is a trap and cost several takes: Sign out clears
> only the delegate, the dialog then offers "Forget identity" where Sign out was,
> the dialog changes height between the two, and the control that opens it only
> exists while signed in. `reset_browser.js` clears `FlutterSecureStorage*` from
> localStorage and verifies both keys absent instead.

### Taps, and why they need a sync flash

Android's `show_touches` is off — its plain dot doesn't match the styled indicator.
`shoot_signin.js` logs every tap (time and device pixel) and `overlay_taps.js`
composites `tapfx/` frames onto them.

> **`screenrecord` keeps capturing for seconds after the process spawns**, so a
> clock zeroed at spawn runs ~4s ahead of the footage and every indicator lands
> early. The script paints the screen white briefly and zeroes there;
> `find_flash.js` finds that frame by luma and returns the offset. Do not replace
> this with a tuned constant.

`overlay_taps.js` also trims everything before the flash — that head is staging,
not video — and starts each indicator 0.24s early so the finger arrives *onto* the
control rather than appearing after it has already reacted.

> `tapfx/` is generated and gitignored: run `node tapframes.js` after a fresh
> clone, or `overlay_taps.js` will fail.

### Never add a sleep to "let it settle"

A six-second sleep after the launch tap was most of a thirty-second take, sitting
immediately before a `waitFor` that already did the job. Worse, it prompted a
speed-ramping step to hide the dead time it had created. Removing it took the take
under nine seconds at real speed, and the ramping step was deleted. If something
needs waiting on, wait on the condition.

### Keep the raw take

Speed-ramped cuts make real latency look better than it is. The unedited take is
what tells you how it actually feels, and re-cutting from it costs nothing —
whereas deleting it means a full re-shoot, which has already happened once.

## 5. Deterministic starting state

A sign-in take needs the phone **vouched, no delegate yet** — otherwise the app
offers to rotate an existing delegate instead of creating one, and the beat the
whole sequence exists for never happens.

There is no fixture generator. The demo identity is one created on a real phone
(filmed anyway, in the shot where the camera sees the identity on the desk), and
its token goes in `tools/intro_video/demo_identity.json`.

Three places hold the state, and all three must be cleared:

| State | Where | Reset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| delegate **statement** | published, one-of-us.net | `truncate_statements.js --prod --keep <first>` with `I_MEAN_IT=yes` |
| delegate **key** | identity app secure storage | `keymeid://deletekey?domain=nerdster.org` |
| identity + delegate **in the browser** | page storage, "Store keys" is ticked | `reset_browser.js` |

> The browser one is the silent killer: the app never prompts because the page is
> already signed in, and the take records something plausible but wrong. Doing it
> through the UI needs two steps whose positions shift between them, so
> `reset_browser.js` clears `FlutterSecureStorage*` from localStorage and then
> verifies both keys absent.

**Truncation refuses any key not listed in `demo_identity.json`**, before a
connection is opened. Everything else in those stores belongs to a real person
and deletion cannot be undone. `--prod` additionally requires `I_MEAN_IT=yes`.

> Statements are a hash chain: each carries `previous`, and the stream document
> holds `head`/`headTime`. Deleting documents without rewinding the head leaves
> the next write failing with `chain race: expected <gone>`. The tool does both.

### Statement tokens

SHA1 of the **pretty-printed** canonical JSON (2-space indent), not the compact
form. Computing from compact JSON gives tokens that match nothing.


## 6. Post

### Speech bubbles — `tools/intro_video/bubbles.js`

Rendered in a headless browser as full-frame transparent PNGs, composited by ffmpeg, one
faded overlay per cue. CSS does the layout, so fonts, fills, shadows and tail geometry are
real design rather than subtitle-renderer approximations.

Each cue names an **anchor** — the point on the frame it is about — and grows a pointer to it:

- **Tail** for a near anchor (≤ `TAIL_MAX`, 240px): tapered, slightly curved.
- **Leader line + ring** for a far one. A tail stretched across half the frame reads as a
  black spike laid over the UI. Both were tried; the spike is why the rule exists.

Styles: `narrator` (dark slab, **Inter**, thin blue rule) and `milhouse` (cream, **Comic
Neue**, dark border) — both fonts the ones `web/index.html` already loads, so the video
matches the site. `fetch_fonts.sh` pulls them.

> Give a style an explicit `pointer` colour. The leader first inherited the narrator bubble's
> `border`, a near-transparent white meant as a subtle edge on a dark fill — invisible as a
> line over the light UI.

> **Anchors are coordinates, not element references.** There's no DOM inside a Flutter canvas,
> so positions are read off frames and hardcoded. They're correct only for that take; a
> re-record shifts the scroll and the tails drift.

### Captions (older path) — ASS subtitles

`captions/*.ass`, burned by `build.sh`. Can't draw a tail; keep only for plain captions.

> In libass, `BorderStyle: 3` boxes are filled with **`OutlineColour`**, not `BackColour`.
> Setting `BackColour` looks right and silently gives a white box.

### Visible finger (web only)

`lib/touch.js` injects a `pointer-events:none` overlay driven by the page's real touch
events, so it can't drift out of sync. It chases the true position on a rAF loop rather than
snapping, leaves a fading motion trail, and ripples on release. The swipe lands, dwells, and
is released while still moving so Flutter applies its own fling, with a slight sideways
drift — a perfectly vertical stroke looks machine-drawn.

### Speed ramps and assembly

Dead air gets cut and ramped rather than performed slowly. The 45s sign-in became 14.9s:
1× for the tap, 2× through the app, 4× through the wait, 1× for the payoff — segments built
separately with `setpts` and joined with `concat`.

### Finding beats

```bash
ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf "fps=1,drawtext=text='%{eif\:n\:d}s':x=8:y=8:fontsize=60:\
fontcolor=yellow:box=1:boxcolor=black@0.8,scale=160:-1,tile=8x6" -frames:v 1 sheet.png
```

A timestamped contact sheet is the fastest way to locate a moment in a long take.

### Voice

`tools/intro_video/setup_tts.sh` installs both, no root needed:

- **Piper** (neural, local) for narration — voices in `voices/`, samples in
  `~/Videos/intro_video_demos/voice_casting.mp4`.
- **espeak-ng** — deliberately synthetic; candidate voice for the demo phone, which is not a
  person and whom nobody has vouched for. Installed by unpacking `.deb`s locally
  (`espeak.sh` wraps it) because there's no passwordless sudo.

`vo.py` reads an ASS/JSON cue list, synthesises each line, staggers overlapping speech so
lines don't collide, and muxes. It reports lines that land late — which is how we learned the
copy runs long against its beats.

> No Claude-side speech synthesis exists; these are local engines. A **Milhouse voice** is out
> regardless — Fox's character, Pamela Hayden's performance. Text bubbles in his register are
> fine.

## 8. Open problems

1. ~~Reset to "vouched, no delegate"~~ — solved, but it is a **three**-part reset (§9).
2. ~~Nerdster footage doesn't look like a browser~~ — solved by shooting in the AVD (§9).
   The drawn `chromebar` is retired; its generator is in `attic/` if a desktop rig ever
   returns.
3. ~~Two touch indicators~~ — solved: `show_touches` off, styled frames composited (§9).
4. **AVD disk can't be grown** without a wipe. Editing `disk.dataPartition.size` does
   nothing to an existing image. Currently ~776 MB free of 6 GB; `pm trim-caches` when an
   install fails.
5. **Caption timings are coupled to a take.** Re-record and cues drift.
6. ~~The shoot script can't see the screen~~ — solved. Flutter's accessibility tree turns
   on with a real touch at the "Enable accessibility" placeholder's **centre** (a corner tap
   silently does nothing), and `lib/semantics.js` then gives tap-by-name, wait-on-state and
   assert. Works against production with no build flag. The identity app half is still
   blind: native Flutter surfaces nodes only through an Android accessibility service.

7. **Timing marks need a sync flash.** `screenrecord` keeps capturing for seconds after the
   process spawns, so a clock zeroed at spawn runs ~4s ahead of the footage and every touch
   indicator lands early. The script paints the screen white briefly and zeroes there;
   `find_flash.js` locates that frame and `overlay_taps.js` shifts by it. Do not replace
   this with a tuned constant.

8. **Never add a sleep to "let it settle".** A six-second sleep after the launch tap was
   most of a thirty-second take, sitting immediately before a `waitFor` that already did the
   job — and it prompted a speed-ramping step to hide the dead time it created. Removing it
   took the take to under nine seconds at real speed. Wait on conditions.
